source.behavior: The source requires UsersManage, validates an 8+ character uppercase/lowercase/numeric password and exact confirmation, persists the reset, clears the account lockout, revokes the target user's sessions, audits Password.Reset without password material, and only then reports success. The UI requires an explicit identity confirmation before invoking the reset.

laravel_adaptation.behavior: A members.manage tenant administrator selects an already tenant-scoped membership, provides a policy-compliant new password plus confirmation, and types the target member email as an independent server-verified confirmation identity. The mutation persists the password, revokes every database session for the target user, writes a redacted immutable tenant audit event, commits, then performs a fresh tenant-scoped membership/user reread and Hash::check before returning success.

authorization.foreign_tenant_semantics: 404 because TenantMembership uses the active tenant global scope
authorization.direct_id_semantics: Only a membership ID from the active tenant is accepted. user_id, tenant_id, and membership_id body fields are prohibited and cannot override server-derived ownership.

validation.password: required string, minimum 8 characters, mixed uppercase/lowercase, at least one number, and Laravel confirmed
validation.confirmation_identity: required string, maximum 255 characters, compared server-side to the tenant-scoped target user's email after membership resolution
validation.failure_semantics: 422 validation responses leave the credential, target sessions, and password-reset audit state unchanged

csrf.route: The mutation is registered in the web middleware group and therefore uses Laravel's CSRF boundary.
csrf.frontend: apiRequest sends same-origin credentials and the current meta csrf-token as X-CSRF-TOKEN.

tenant_isolation.proof: The target User ID is never accepted from the caller. It is derived from a TenantMembership resolved under the active TenantContext. A direct foreign membership ID returns 404 before any credential/session/audit mutation.

secret_boundary.password_input: Password fields use password inputs and are cleared after every mutation attempt.
secret_boundary.server_response: Only membership id, safe user identity fields, password_changed, and revoked_sessions are returned. Plaintext and password hash are never serialized.
secret_boundary.audit: Audit metadata contains target_user_id and revoked_sessions only and is passed through the standard Redactor. It never receives password or password hash values.
secret_boundary.logging: No password material is logged or added to operation/audit payloads.

persistence.transaction: Password persistence, target-session revocation, and immutable audit creation occur in one database transaction.
persistence.authoritative_reread: After the transaction commits, the service re-resolves the same membership through the active tenant scope, verifies the same target user identity, and Hash::check verifies the newly persisted credential before success is returned.
persistence.source_lockout_note: The Laravel User model has no persisted source-equivalent lockout counters to clear. This operation does not fabricate a lockout-clear claim; target session revocation and password reset semantics are implemented truthfully.

retry_idempotency_cancellation.idempotency: Password reset is an intentional non-idempotent security mutation because each accepted submission writes a new credential hash and audit event.
retry_idempotency_cancellation.retry: TanStack mutation retry is explicitly false and the submit control is disabled while pending; a retry requires a fresh explicit user action and re-entry of cleared password fields.
retry_idempotency_cancellation.cancellation: The runtime mutation is synchronous and transactional with no queued job or cancellable background operation; no fake cancellation surface is exposed.

no_fake_success.proof: No demo/sample branch exists. Success depends on real database persistence, session deletion, audit insertion, transaction commit, and post-commit Hash::check on an authoritative reread.
